title: Load the FX rate card once for every thread

blocks.text: The FX service prices every request from a rate card it fetches from an upstream that answers slowly and allows a handful of requests a minute. The card is wrapped in one shared `Supplier<RateCard>` that all request threads call. After a deploy the upstream rejected the service for a minute: the first burst of requests had each fetched the card. Some desks have no card at all, and their source answers `null`. When the upstream is briefly down at startup, the service must keep trying on later requests rather than stay broken, and it must start without calling the upstream.

Write `get()` in `src/main/java/practice/Once.java`, adding the fields it needs. When you're done, the source runs once for all threads, on the first request, whatever it returns, and a load that throws is tried again by the next caller. About twelve lines in total.
The tests call `get()` from a thread pool, and hold a load in progress with a latch while a second caller arrives.

cases.says: calls one after another all get the object the first call loaded, and the source runs once
constructing the object does not call the source; the first get() does
a caller that arrives while the first load is still running gets that load's value instead of starting another
a source that returns null is still called only once
a load that throws passes the exception to its caller and is tried again on the next call

origin.section: A Safe Memo Chooses What It Pays: a Lock, Class Initialisation, or Startup Time

concepts: Double-checked locking with a volatile flag loads once, keeps a null result, and retries after a failed load.
A check-then-compute memo without a lock lets two threads that arrive together both run the load.
